<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|242|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VIII.}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. VIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Againe in the Temple (absoluing an aduoutresse after his merciful maner, and yet vvithal declaring against his enemies that he is not a fauourer of sinne, no more then Moyses) 12 he teacheth openly, and is not for al that apprehended. telling them both of his Godhead, 21 and of their reprobation, 28 of his exaltation also by their Crucifying of him. 31 exhorting the beleeuers to perseuére: 33 and shewing them that seeke his death, that they are neither free, 39 nor of Abraham, 41 nor of God, 44 but of the Diuel. 45 but that him selfe is of God, 52 and greater and auncienter then Abraham. 59 For the which they goe about to stone him, but in vaine.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=8|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Saturday the 3 Weeke of Lent.}}{{sc|Iesvs}} vvent into the Mount-oliuet: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=2}}† and early in the morning againe he came into the temple, and the people came to him, and sitting he taught them. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=3}}† And the Scribes and Pharisees bring a vvoman taken in aduoutrie: and they did set her in the middes, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=4}}† and said to him, Maister, this vvoman vvas euen novv taken in aduoutrie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=5}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 20, 10.''}}* in the lavv Moyses commaunded vs to stone such. What saiest thou therfore? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=6}}† And this they said tempting him: that they might accuse him. But {{sc|Iesvs}} bovving him self dovvne, vvith his finger vvrote in the earth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=7}}† VVhen they therfore continued asking him: he lifted vp him self, and said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We can not conueniently reprehend or condemne other mens faults, if our selues be guilty of the same or other greater. ''Cyril in Io. See Annot. Mt. 7, 1''.}}∷ He that is vvithout sinne of you, let him first throvv the stone at her. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=8}}† And againe bovving him self, he vvrote in the earth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=9}}† And they hearing, went out one by one, beginning at the seniours: and {{sc|Iesvs}} alone remained, and the vvoman standing in the middes. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=10}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} lifting vp him self, said to her, VVoman, vvhere are they that accused thee? hath no man condemned thee? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=11}}† VVho said, No man, Lord. And {{sc|Iesvs}} said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Augustine by this example of our Maister proueth that Clergie men specially should be giuen much to mercie: and that they ought often, as the cause and time require, to get pardon of the secular Magistrates for offenders that be penitent. ''Ep. 54''.}}∷ Neither vvil I condemne thee. Goe, and novv sinne no more.⊣

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon Saturday the 4 weeke in Lent.}}b Againe therfore {{sc|Iesvs}} spake to them, saying, I am the light of the vvorld. he that folovveth me, vvalketh not in darkenesse: but shal haue the light of life. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=13}}† The Pharisees therfore said to him, Thou giuest testimonie of thy self: thy testimonie is not true. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to them, Although I doe giue testimonie of my self, my testimonie is true: because I knovv vvhence I came, & vvhither I goe: but you knovv not whence I come, or whither I goe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}}† You iudge according to the flesh: I doe not iudge any man. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}}† And if I doe iudge, my iudgement is true: because I am not alone, but I and he that sent me, the Father. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}}† And in your lavv it is vvritten, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 17, 6. 19, 15.''}}* the testimonie of tvvo men is true. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}}† I am he that giue testimonie of my self: and he that sent me, the Father, giueth testimonie of me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}}† They said therfore to him, VVhere is thy father? {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, Neither me doe you knovv, nor my Father. If you did knovv me: perhaps you might knovv my Father also. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† These vvordes {{sc|Iesvs}} spake in the Treasurie, teaching in the temple: and no man apprehended him, because his houre vvas not yet come.⊣<noinclude>{{rh|||† Againe}}</noinclude>
